Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $2-\sqrt{3}$:

$$\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2+\sqrt{3}}=\frac{(1+\sqrt{2})(2-\sqrt{3})}{4-3}=2-\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{6}.$$

Group the terms to match $A(1+\sqrt{B})-(\sqrt{C}+\sqrt{D})$ with $A=2$:

$$2(1+\sqrt{2})-(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{6}) = 2+2\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{6}.$$

This matches, so $A=2$, $B=2$, $C=3$, $D=6$, and

$$A+B+C+D=2+2+3+6=13.$$

ANSWER: 13
